no_session_rows_since_2026_09_01_charact.note_on_uas: None of these match KNOWN_BOT_UA_PATTERN (bot-detection.ts) — they are current, realistic, diverse browser UAs (Chrome 142-150, Edge, Safari, mobile Safari), which is why UA-based detection cannot catch this traffic class.
no_session_rows_since_2026_09_01_charact.note_on_referrer: The ExitLink/CategoryExitLink anchors carry rel="noopener noreferrer" and every real click additionally re-opens the URL via window.open(url,'_blank','noopener,noreferrer') — so a genuine click, whether or not its onClick JS runs, should send NO referrer at all. A referrer of the bare origin (no path) is therefore itself evidence AGAINST these being real clicks through this element, not for it: it indicates a client that does not honor rel=noreferrer, i.e. a non-browser HTTP client.
no_session_rows_since_2026_09_01_charact.note_on_store_names: store_name is stamped as String(resolved.storeId) by src/app/go/[offerId]/route.ts for every /go request — the numeric values above are NOT a bot signature, they are the normal value this route always writes. The small Arabic-named rows come from a separate, older insert path (per category-exit-link.tsx's own comment about a 'plain, zero-JS <a>' still in use on parts of /compare) — not investigated further, out of this mission's scope.
no_session_rows_since_2026_09_01_charact.note_on_timing: Sharp bursts at hour 23 (831) and hour 11 (500), well above neighboring hours — consistent with a scheduled crawl job rather than ambient organic traffic, which would follow a smoother daily usage curve.

still_active_check.conclusion: Not fully stopped, but far below the 2026-09-02 peak (1886/day ≈ 78/hour) — has tapered to roughly the same order of magnitude as the pre-spike August baseline, possibly slightly above it.

root_cause.classification: EXTERNAL — an automated HTTP client (crawler/scraper class, exact identity not determined) directly requesting the /go/[offerId] route.
root_cause.mechanism: src/components/catalog/exit-link.tsx (ExitLink) and src/components/catalog/category-exit-link.tsx (CategoryExitLink) render a real, crawlable <a href="/go/<offerId>"> in server-rendered HTML — kept deliberately for accessibility/no-JS/middle-click support. A real user's click is intercepted by onClick (preventDefault + window.open with tracked session/interaction params). A non-JS HTTP client that simply parses the HTML and follows the raw href bypasses the onClick handler entirely, hitting the route directly with a plain GET — receiving a normal 302 redirect and a normal outbound_clicks row, with none of the client-side session/interaction stamping. This exact failure mode was already predicted in the /go route's own ADR-286 comment ('a crawler, curl, a scraper — no click, no JS, no session required... receives an identically valid token').
root_cause.contributing_factor: robots.txt already disallows /go/ for all user agents, but this traffic does not honor it — either a non-compliant crawler, or a compliant-with-robots.txt-format but not enforcing client (many link-checker/SEO-audit/preview tools use realistic modern UAs specifically to avoid being blocked).
root_cause.not_the_cause: isKnownBotUserAgent()'s existing UA allowlist (bot-detection.ts) — correctly flags its own known signatures (175 rows this window) but this traffic uses realistic, non-matching UAs.
root_cause.not_the_cause_2: store_name being a numeric string — this is the route's own normal, by-design behavior for every request, not evidence of anything unusual on its own.

fix_applied.boundary: SESSION_TRACKING_LIVE_SINCE = 2026-08-13T09:08:15Z (the verified-live instant the earliest session_id-populated row exists) — a row with no session_id is only classified as probable-automated if it was written AT OR AFTER this instant, so pre-cutover historical rows (which legitimately have no session_id because the column didn't exist yet) are never misclassified.
fix_applied.scope: Applied only to the retailer-facing (merchant-conversation) report, not to the general Command Center funnel/KPIs — narrower scope, lower risk, matches this mission's explicit priority (make merchant-facing evidence defensible). Extending the same classifier to command-center-queries.ts's broader consumers is a reasonable, separate follow-up, not done in this pass.
fix_applied.not_fixed_this_pass: The exact identity/operator of the automated client was not determined (no further network-level investigation attempted — out of scope for a read-only DB/code investigation). A full audit of every exit-link rendering surface for the same raw-href pattern (beyond exit-link.tsx and category-exit-link.tsx) was not exhaustively completed.
